rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The clock is on the CLAIM, not the source's age — durable-account carve-out.
rules_evaluated.evidence: BOUNDARY CASE, resolved PASS on harm-absence, not on a clean textual match — flagged for maintainer attention as a TODO, not blocked. §2a's three literal conditions (first-hand; SPECIFIC COMPLETED EVENT, not a practice/trend/rate; dated in body) describe a lived episode ("a run that took ten hours"), and this citation instead backs a framework/step-definition attribution — a materially different claim shape the rule's literal text does not name. Applying the rule's own diagnostic ("would re-checking it next year change the answer?"): re-opening the every.to page in 2027 will not change whether Shipper & Klaassen named these two steps 'Review' and 'Compound' in that Dec-2025 piece — that fact is fixed the way a completed-and-dated publication act is fixed, not a moving-world claim like adoption/capability/who-currently-believes-what. The stamp itself does the §2b-required scoping work ("due:none on the DATED-ORIGIN VARIANT, since a step definition's publication does not expire and the body never claims it as current practice") and the backing block's own fallback confirms nothing downstream load-bears on Klaassen's continued relevance ("teach the two-run review without the name; the move stands on the student's own artefacts", Sources line 132) — so the harm §2a/§2 exist to prevent (a claim about a moving world quietly aging past its check-by date while curriculum keeps citing it as current) is not present on this specific citation. Per _dispatch-preamble.md's evidence-of-harm clause: harm absent → PASS + rule question, not REVISE. TODO filed below recommending §2a's text explicitly name 'framework/definitional-origin attribution' as a fourth durable shape alongside 'specific completed event,' since the current wording leaves this exact case ambiguous on a strict reading (a prior pass on THIS same citation, before the due:none fix existed, read the ambiguity the other way and marked N/A with reasoning that — read today — would argue against the carve-out applying).
